beats: Last week, a ship fell back from orbit… and a tower caught it.
Why not just land on legs? Because the tower is the landing gear.
Legs ride all the way to space and back. Every single flight.
On the upper stage, every kilo of legs is a kilo of cargo left behind.
So the ship comes down tail first, hovering on its engines beside the tower.
Two giant arms, nicknamed the chopsticks, slide to its height and swing closed.
Two small pins near the top rest on the arms. That's all the landing gear it carries.
The heavy, strong parts stay on the ground, where weight costs nothing.
The engines shut down, and the arms hold the full weight of the empty ship.
And it lands right where it launches. No barge, no truck, no long trip home.
The same arms can lift it back onto a booster for the next flight.
Legs in space are dead weight. A tower on the ground isn't.
